title: Short CUDA Adam feasibility check on the IBM two-hidden-layer MNIST topology
hypothesis: A five-epoch hybrid pulse-Adam run on the published-defect IBM-OM model can approach the reported 97.35% TTv2 accuracy on the 784-256-128-10 sigmoid MNIST network; apparent-state accuracy and teacher KL are the co-primary descriptive metrics, while persistent-state metrics are diagnostics.
motivation: The initial 784-50-10 from-scratch comparison reached 73.4% apparent test accuracy with pulse-Adam after ten epochs and 50.9% with Tiki-Taka. This exploratory successor changes to the two-hidden-layer IBM simulation topology, uses the paper-compatible raw [0,1] MNIST input and sigmoid nonlinearities, drops Tiki-Taka, and reduces the budget to five epochs. A matched digital Adam control separates optimizer/architecture capacity from the OM update path.

arms.description: Five epochs of label-supervised hybrid pulse-Adam on one published-defect OM assignment, plus a matched FP32 Adam control.

completion_criteria: The declared config completes exactly once through python -m ebl on CUDA and records the resolved CUDA device before and after training.

The student architecture is 784-256-128-10 with analog biases and digital sigmoid hidden nonlinearities; all 235,146 programmable q states use the native sampled OM bounds with no weight mapping and no [0,2] clipping.
The OM population retains corrupt_devices_prob=0.1348 and corrupt_devices_range=0.01, assignment seed 87004, endpoint seed 89402, and the AIHWKit 1.1.0 model-based OM fit.

Both the OM and digital arms start from byte-identical AIHWKit/PyTorch Linear Kaiming-uniform weights and biases, consume five identically ordered epochs of all 60,000 MNIST training examples in batches of 64, and use fixed epoch 5 without checkpoint selection.

Every training and evaluation forward in the device arm consumes the held apparent q state. Adam moments generate stochastic one-pulse commands that update the hidden persistent q state, after which touched apparent cells are refreshed.

The full official 10,000-example test set is evaluated after every epoch. Fixed epoch-5 apparent accuracy, teacher agreement, and teacher-to-student KL are primary; persistent accuracy and KL are labelled diagnostics.

Comparable accuracy is operationally defined as no more than two percentage points below IBM's reported 97.35% TTv2 result. KL has no IBM reference and is compared only against the matched digital Adam control.

This one-seed, one-assignment, five-epoch Adam run remains exploratory and is not promoted as a reproduction of IBM's median-of-five, 100-epoch, optimized-TTv2 result. It retains the same AIHWKit preset default reference_std=0.05 as the prior crossbar tests, whereas Fig. 13 of the paper states a 1% symmetry-point reference-write assumption.
analysis_plan: Verify the matched digital arm reaches high accuracy; otherwise diagnose initialization, raw-input preprocessing, architecture, or Adam settings before attributing any gap to OM devices.
Report per-epoch apparent and persistent accuracy/KL, commanded pulses by layer, defect fraction, and saturation/programming diagnostics.

Compare fixed epoch-5 apparent accuracy with the 95.35% comparability gate, IBM's 97.35% TTv2 result, and the matched digital endpoint. Compare apparent KL with matched digital KL without inventing an IBM KL benchmark.
If the digital arm is healthy but the OM arm misses the gate, treat this as evidence about this short hybrid-Adam recipe only; do not infer that the IBM TTv2 simulation is irreproducible.
